Because `DIRECTIVE_RE` (mermaid.ts:187) has an optional `(?:}%{2})?` and a greedy `((?:(?!}%{2}).|\r?\n)*)`, the unterminated directive strips to the end of the fence, so `source` here is (near) empty — the assertion would pass for `stripConfigDirectives = () => ''`. finding.summary: The editor→preview palette wiring (`preview.setTheme(mode)`) has no test; both new editor tests pass if that line is deleted
finding.evidence: editor.ts:440-443 adds two behaviours on a theme switch: (a) repaint the preview, (b) push the new palette into NotePreview so mermaid re-renders in the new colours. The two new tests in editor.test.ts (`repaints the preview on a theme switch while it is visible`, `skips the theme repaint while the preview is hidden`) detect only (a) — they insert a `[data-role="repaint-marker"]` span and assert it is/isn't wiped, plus `querySelector('h1')`. Neither test stubs a mermaid loader or inspects the preview's mermaid theme, so removing `preview.setTheme(mode)` (leaving only `renderPreview()`) keeps both green while diagrams keep the stale palette — exactly the user-visible bug the comment says the change exists to prevent. preview.test.ts covers `NotePreview.setTheme` in isolation, but nothing covers the editor calling it.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the editor→preview palette wiring (`preview.setTheme(mode)` at editor.ts:442) has no test and that deleting it leaves the new editor tests green. A third new editor test exists that covers exactly this: editor.test.ts:216-239 "pushes the new palette into the preview on a theme switch" spies on `NotePreview.prototype.setTheme` (line 219, with NotePreview imported at line 5) and asserts `toHaveBeenCalledWith('dark')` after `api.setTheme('dark')` (lines 225-226). Removing editor.ts:442 fails that assertion, so the mutation the finding claims survives is in fact caught. The test further pins direction with `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('light')` (line 230) and the same-theme no-op guard (editor.ts:433) with `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` (line 232). The spy is a bare `vi.spyOn` with no mockImplementation and is restored in a `finally`, so the real method still executes — not over-mocking. The other half of the behavior (palette actually reaching mermaid, cache busted on theme change) is covered non-vacuously in preview.test.ts:658-673 against a stub engine, asserting `engine.initialize` last called with `theme: 'dark'` and `engine.render` called twice. The reviewer's own stated search (grep setTheme across packages/notes/src) would have returned editor.test.ts:219-232, so the premise is factually wrong.
